title: Decode: low-latency dense GEMM family (BF16 + MXFP8)
shape: D3-32 r24: 96 requests / DP rank (384 verify rows R per TP4 group, n = 96 SP shard rows per GPU), L=135K, k=3
basis: baseline/current: gap512 EP16 in-step BF16 family (mxfp4 tree, all-BF16 linears). achievable: perf model nvfp4_modelopt D3-32 r24 (model_gemm.py), my ops = KDA in/f_b/o_proj, DSA qkv_a+g_proj, q_b+wq_b, DSA o_proj, router, latent down/up, shared gate_up/down (w_uk/w_uv bmm excluded: MLA q path). mxfp4-tree achievable for the same ops = 4.60 ms.
gap_analysis: Seed (gap512 B50-B92, EP16): weight-streaming GEMMs at M=32-384 reach 1.8-8.7 TB/s vs 13.9 achievable; cuBLAS picks 2-CTA 64xN / 160x64 tiles with 156-448 CTAs; split-K reduce launches ~1.2 ms/step; a CuTe SplitKGemm collapses above 200 rows. Under the NVFP4 checkpoint the KDA in/o_proj and shared experts become MXFP8 (half the weight bytes), but the sdec SP path refuses quantized linears today (providers.bf16_weight), so D3-32 NVFP4 decode cannot run at all until B4 lands. Re-measuring every family at the D3-32 per-GPU shapes (R=16/128/256/384, n=4/32/64/96) for BF16 tactics and all MXFP8 backends (FI cute-dsl / cutlass / trtllm, cuBLASLt _scaled_mm) is the first step.
inefficiencies: Too few bytes in flight per SM for 30-180 MB weight streams (cuBLAS tile choice) [seed, to re-measure on D3-32 shapes]
SplitKGemm tile policy collapse above 200 rows (identity unverified) [seed]
MXFP8 activation quant as separate kernels (NVFP4 ckpt) [seed]

rubin_features: tcgen05 block-scaled MXFP8 MMA (swap-AB, weight as the M operand)
TMA bulk loads / L2 prefetch of the next GEMM's weights
plan: 1. Microbench every family at D3-32 per-GPU shapes: BF16 tactic table vs cuBLAS/Lt; MXFP8 FI cute-dsl/cutlass/trtllm vs _scaled_mm (+ act quant), chained cold weights in a CUDA graph; compare to model achievable
2. B4: MXFP8 DecodeProjection (per-shape backend dispatch, pre-quantized MXFP8 input from fused producers) + MXFP8 SpOproj + MXFP8 SpMlp shared expert inside specialized_decode; unit tests vs stock
3. Weight-streaming kernel redesign for families still > 1.1x achievable (persistent swap-AB, PDL weight prefetch, no separate reduce)
4. Step A/B on INFRA's 1-node harness; landed-ready
